title: 3 tips for getting the best deals this holiday shopping season
summary: With the ever-changing landscape of holiday shopping, how do you know you're getting the best deal?

title: The holiday season can be expensive. Here are some tips for keeping credit card debt in check
summary: About 76% of people who said they would throw down money this holiday season identified at least one reason they might overspend, including fear of missing out or not spending enough time planning, a NerdWallet survey found.

title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed to Saturday due to expected bad weather
summary: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed as powerful winds are expected to bear down on New York during the annual event, NBC said Wednesday.

title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to celebrate a milestone with Blue Hippo, Bluey and Megan Moroney
summary: One of the stars of this year's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade should be very easy to spot. Just look in the sky for a gigantic blue hippo with a goofy smile.

title: State Department reports downplay violence and corruption in countries that asylum seekers are fleeing
summary: The reports use cherry-picked data, careful phrasing and in some cases facts that don't stand up to scrutiny to create misleading depictions of countries that are in fact often plagued by violence, government corruption and police inaction.

title: Ábrego García, a Salvadoran mistakenly deported by U.S., goes to Spain but hopes to return after Trump
summary: Kilmar Ábrego García, a Salvadoran national who fought his mistaken deportation from the United States, arrived in Spain on Wednesday after what his lawyer described as a temporary departure, with hopes of returning to his family's home in Maryland after President Donald Trump leaves office.

title: Alaska ends voter data agreement with Justice Department, which had been searching for noncitizens
summary: A Republican official who oversees Alaska elections said she has ended an agreement under which the state shared its voter registration list with the U.S. Department of Justice and allowed the agency to flag voters for possible removal.

title: Georgia's Fulton County ordered to give copy of 2020 election records seized by FBI to state board
summary: A judge on Tuesday ordered Georgia's Fulton County to turn over a digital copy of ballots and other election records seized by the FBI earlier this year to the State Election Board, which had been trying for more than two years to obtain certain records from the 2020 election in the state's most populous county.

title: These young Republicans have a message for their party: It's time to 'grow up'
summary: Three weeks after midterm elections that devastated the Republican Party, several dozen of its more youthful members gathered at a brewery to sort through the pieces.

title: WATCH: Vance defends Iowa lead azide detonation as he visits Air Force troops in Ohio
summary: Vice President JD Vance, second lady Usha Vance and their four children visited Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio on Wednesday, serving a Thanksgiving meal to troops and joining them for lunch.

title: Ben Shapiro and Amna Nawaz discuss GOP's future on 'Settle In'
summary: Political commentator Ben Shapiro has been a prominent and often controversial force in conservative media since he was a teenager. Now in his early 40s, he hosts one of America's most popular podcasts and remains editor emeritus of The Daily Wire. Amna Nawaz sat down with Shapiro on "Settle In" to discuss the GOP's path forward after the midterms and other hot-button issues.

title: Cranberry farmers forced to adapt as climate change threatens harvest
summary: Cranberries are a Thanksgiving fixture, and the United States produces most of the world's supply. But growing them relies on a narrow window of time with the right conditions. With climate change, those conditions are shifting. For our Tipping Point series, special correspondent Ben Tracy with Climate Central shows us how scientists and growers are working to save the seasonal favorite.

title: Former Israeli generals protect Palestinians from settler attacks during olive harvest
summary: This week, Palestinians in the occupied West Bank are concluding their annual olive harvest, one that the U.N. says has been the most violent on record. In the first of two stories from Nick Schifrin and his team in the West Bank, he looks at how some Israeli settlers have dramatically increased their attacks on Palestinians, and what that says about a battle within Israel over its own future.

title: From her apartment, photographer captures unique view of Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
summary: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed to Saturday due to severe weather. When the balloons rise above Manhattan, few will have the same view of the spectacle as Elizabeth Kahane. The New York photographer has been capturing images of the parade from her apartment for almost three decades. Stephanie Sy reports.

title: How Trump's newest tariffs could impact Americans and the economy
summary: The Trump administration announced plans for a new round of tariffs on China, the European Union and 12 other major trading partners. China would face the highest rate with a new 20% tariff on most products. To discuss how this will impact Americans and the economy, Lisa Desjardins spoke with Gavin Bade of The Wall Street Journal.

title: Meet the young maestro leading the Chicago Symphony Orchestra
summary: The Chicago Symphony Orchestra has long been considered one of the nation's leading classical music ensembles. Led by a series of celebrated conductors, it's now turning to a new artistic leader who was just 28 when the announcement came. Senior arts correspondent Jeffrey Brown met Klaus Mäkelä as he gets to know his new orchestra. It's part of our arts and culture series, CANVAS.

title: News Wrap: Severe weather threatens holiday travel for millions
summary: In our news wrap Wednesday, severe weather is threatening Thanksgiving travel for millions of Americans, authorities in Egypt say at least 30 are dead after a crash involving a fuel tanker sparked a massive fire near Cairo and the Treasury Department's financial crimes enforcement network suffered what it calls a "cybersecurity incident."

title: What the Army's Iowa detonation means for nearby communities
summary: The Army blew up a highly volatile lead chemical compound in Iowa after a federal court gave the green light. Officials called the operation a success, but did not take questions from reporters. Surrounding communities remain on alert, and three states say they're monitoring the effects. Stephanie Sy reports, and Lisa Desjardins discusses more with Eliza Billingham of Iowa Public Radio.

title: Melania Trump reunites her seventh group of Ukrainian and Russian children with their families
summary: First lady Melania Trump has helped return a seventh group of Ukrainian and Russian children to their families, bringing the total number of kids in these wartime reunifications to 43, the White House announced Wednesday.
